title: The Location of the Fragment
text: “You can’t do that! If you do something like that, it’ll be all for nothing!”
Just as I was about to leave the room to wake up my Assistant, Rival shouted at me.
“Motoyasu, don’t do that—the other person clearly doesn’t want you to.”
“But Father, my Assistant will be delighted to know this guy is still alive.”
“Well, that’s true. Hey, aren’t you going to change your mind?”
“No way!”
“I see… Well then, Motoyasu, since he is Wyndia-chan’s father after all, wouldn’t it be best to respect his parenting style?”
Father said this in a lecturing tone. I have my own thoughts on the matter, but if it’s coming from Father, I suppose I have no choice.
“I understand.”
“Well, let’s put this issue on hold for now. How about we work together to get stronger? I’ve already raised Gaelion-chan’s level to a certain extent, though?”
“That alone isn’t enough. You two must have slain several Dragon Emperors in other countries. I’d like you to hand over the Core Stones you obtained back then.”
“Fine, whatever… What’s in it for us?”
“First, I need to explain what dragons actually are.”

And with that, Rival began rattling off details about dragon ecology. Apparently, the Dragon Emperor species starts out as a single individual and inherits its memories through the Dragon Core Stone. Then, due to past battles, the Dragon Emperor’s Core Stones were scattered, and they’re said to be trying to reunite into one.
“As the true Dragon Emperor, I wish to engage in Gathering and grow stronger.”
“Well… I’ll help as long as you cooperate, but are there any other benefits?”
“Hmm, the method for breaking through limits and performing Class Up—the one the Spear Hero from the future mentioned—is likely hidden within those scattered Core Stones as well.”
“I see… So that’s what Motoyasu-kun was talking about.”
“That’s right.”
“Hmm… I suppose it’s necessary if we’re going to survive what lies ahead. As an investment in the future, I don’t really have a reason to refuse…”
It’s frustrating, but you’re absolutely right. If we can break through the level cap, Filolial-sama and the others—including Keel—should grow into fully capable combatants.
“There’s also a Class Up that grants the Dragon’s Blessing.”
“Oh, so dragons have one too?”
I’ve already mentioned the Class Up offered by the Great Filolial-sama, who is, after all, Her Majesty the Queen. But a Class Up from a dragon? It makes me want to vomit.
“I, too, believe I can build a good relationship with you lot.”

What a despicable creature—presenting a reason I can’t refuse. But since it’s just me and Father, there’s a limit to how much we can level up our party members. Of course, we could get by with improving their aptitudes, but some improvements can’t be made until after level 100, so it’s a bit of a dilemma. If we’re thinking about the future… well.
“That said, everyone’s already undergone Class Up, right? But I hear there’s a level reset coming, so maybe we should time it right.”
“Hmm, I’ll leave the timing up to you.”
“So? Does Motoyasu-kun know where the Dragon Cores for breaking through the level cap are?”
“I do, indeed.”
“Well, my memory’s pretty fuzzy on that… Wait, you actually know?”
It seems my Father was planning to talk as if my memory were fuzzy.
“So where is it?”
“Currently, it’s in the possession of the Dragon Emperor raised by Takt, who’s famous as one of the Seven Star Heroes of Faubrey.”
“It’s already in someone else’s hands…? If I recall correctly from Motoyasu-kun’s story, that dragon’s going to cause quite a ruckus in the future, right?”
“That’s right. From what I heard from my Father and Filolial-sama and the others, that dragon gathered most of the Core Stones after defeating Takt’s dragon, and became a powerful Dragon Emperor.”
“Hmm… So does that mean he’s already gathered them all?”
Rival’s face is turning pale. Just as you’d expect from the weakest Dragon Emperor—I can’t help but laugh at how he’s already backing down.
“Well… I know it’s unlikely we’ll be able to negotiate, but maybe we should still try to see if we can cooperate…? If that doesn’t work, then we’ll fight.”
“That’s the way to go. Don’t worry—with me here, it’ll be one hit. It was one hit in the last loop, after all.”
“So a battle against a Dragon Emperor who’s already gathered all the stones awaits us… It’s amazing that my future self managed to win.”
“I heard you fought alongside Ren and defeated him.”
“With the Sword Hero? What a twist of fate.”
He’s looking down, lost in thought, muttering that his Rival is fate. “Don’t get too full of yourself!” is what I’d say.
“Ah, come to think of it, I’m supposed to meet Ren next, aren’t I?”
“I won’t talk to him. I have no intention of getting along with someone who kills monsters as if it were just a job. I can’t believe my future self actually let him ride on my back.”

“I’m not forcing you to talk to him. In the future, Ren is supposed to grow through various setbacks, but I can’t let him go through that this time. I guess I’ll just have to try to persuade him somehow.”
“That’s a tough one.”

Come to think of it, it’ll be a while before Ren and Itsuki can build a good relationship. The Spirit Tortoise incident was supposed to be the key to that, but even from my perspective, I’d like to avoid a problem that escalates into such a major disaster.

After all, it ended up causing massive casualties, and the Four Holy Heroes faced a lot of backlash afterward. I can’t even imagine what would have happened if my Father hadn’t earned their trust through his steady efforts. In any case, even if I manage to build a good relationship with Ren and Itsuki, if things get complicated here, some very troublesome issues will surface.

Even if Ren and Itsuki end up maturing as people in the end, we’d better think about whether there are any other options. As my Father says, the challenge is how to persuade Ren and Itsuki. The existence of Crimson Swine and Trash, who are driving a wedge between the Heroes, is infuriating. We need to take care of those guys as soon as possible.
“Ren kept saying it was a ‘difference in weapon systems’ even when we showed him the gap in our strength. There’s a high chance he won’t listen even if we demonstrate our power.”
“That’s true.”

Back on Cal Mira Island, neither I, Ren, nor Itsuki believed the enhancement method that Father shared with us using his shadow. Even if we demonstrated it right in front of him, it probably wouldn’t change anything. This time, too, after hearing the enhancement method from Father, Ren mistakenly assumed it was a “difference in weapon systems” and refused to believe it. We need to get him to change his mind somehow, but I haven’t the faintest idea how to go about it.
“That said, considering the battles in the next wave are supposed to be even tougher… well, let’s just think about it once this commotion is over.”
“After the second wave ends, Father and the others will be wanted by the authorities, so we’ll be heading to Cal Mira Island after that incident. There… we’ll just have to get him to believe us.”
“If they hear it from us or our comrades, they might believe us a little. That plan sounds reasonable.”

Just as Father instructed last time, I’ll make good use of my knowledge of the future. So far, things are proceeding without any major issues. It’s true—as Father said, if we act in accordance with that future knowledge, dealing with things becomes much easier.
“Well, enough about Ren for now—isn’t Motoyasu-kun about to start saying he wants a new Filolial?”
“That’s right! As expected of you, Father—you really do understand things well.”
“…We’ve known each other for quite a while now, after all.”
The more Filolial-sama, the better. I’d love to get so many eggs that I can’t even handle them all.
“Well then, since things are going fairly smoothly and we’ve got some extra money, let’s head down to the town below the castle and buy the ones we’ve had set aside at the slave trader’s.”
“I’m looking forward to it.”
“Hmm… We already have plenty, and now you want even more Filolials? I object. They’re too noisy to handle.”
“What’s the matter? Got a problem? I’ll just wipe you out.”
“Those associated with the Filolials always try to solve everything with force, don’t they? It’s utterly lacking in class.”
“Are we getting more Naofumi allies?”
Sakura-chan is tilting her head in confusion. I’m locked in a fierce stare-down with my Rival.

“We’re close, but if worst comes to worst, we could always have them watch the place—it’s not like we’re out of options. There are plenty of things to do, like having them rest over in Siltvelt, so even though they’re not human, we could use all the help we can get.”
“It’s fun when there are a lot of people, isn’t it?”
“Yeah. As it gradually gets livelier, it reminds me of when I used to play online games. That feeling of working together to defeat a great evil is really satisfying.”
Father smiled cheerfully as he said this. Right after that, though, Ren muttered that he could sort of understand why they were mistaking this for a game.
Now that the plague has been contained, it seems the people of the eastern village are on the road to recovery. Father, as if his work here were done, announced his departure.
“Um… Holy One,”
“As I said before, I’d like you to use the reward to rebuild your own village. So that you’ll never again… blame someone else for the mistakes you’ve made yourselves.”
After saying that, Father turned around and added,
“Oh, but be sure to pay the healer a fair reward. Without him, this village might have been wiped out by the plague before we even arrived.”
“Y-yes!”
“Well then, we’ll come back if we get the chance.”
At Father’s signal, Sakura-chan, who was pulling the carriage, started walking.
“Thank you so much!”
The entire village was out waving their hands.
“See ya!”
Keel was waving cheerfully.
Tate and Party’s Good Deeds Points: 35 (12)
